experiences.name: Prague Old Town & Astronomical Clock Tour
experiences.description: Wander through the cobblestone streets of Prague's Old Town Square, marvel at the medieval Astronomical Clock (Orloj) as it chimes on the hour, and explore the Gothic Týn Church. Join a free walking tour to uncover centuries of Bohemian history, Jewish Quarter stories, and Communist-era secrets from a knowledgeable local guide.

experiences.name: Budapest Thermal Bath Experience at Széchenyi
experiences.description: Soak in the iconic neo-baroque Széchenyi Thermal Baths, one of Europe's largest medicinal bath complexes fed by natural hot springs. Enjoy indoor and outdoor pools at varying temperatures, steam rooms, and saunas. A quintessential Budapest ritual practiced by locals for over a century, blending relaxation with rich architectural grandeur.

experiences.name: Prague Local Food Market & Czech Cuisine Tasting
experiences.description: Visit the Manifesto Market or Náplavka Farmers' Market along the Vltava riverbank to sample authentic Czech street food including svíčková (beef sirloin with cream sauce), trdelník pastry, and locally brewed craft beer. Chat with vendors, taste seasonal produce, and experience the vibrant local food culture away from tourist traps.

experiences.name: Budapest Ruin Bar Crawl in the Jewish Quarter
experiences.description: Explore Budapest's legendary ruin bars — abandoned buildings transformed into eclectic, art-filled social hubs. Start at the iconic Szimpla Kert, the original ruin bar, then hop through Instant and Fogas Ház. Sample Hungarian pálinka (fruit brandy) and local craft beers while soaking in the bohemian atmosphere unique to Budapest's nightlife culture.

experiences.name: Buda Castle Hill & Fisherman's Bastion Panorama Walk
experiences.description: Climb or take the historic funicular up to Buda Castle Hill to explore the Royal Palace, Matthias Church, and the fairy-tale turrets of Fisherman's Bastion offering breathtaking panoramic views over the Danube and Pest skyline. Discover over 1,000 years of Hungarian royal history and photograph one of Europe's most dramatic urban vistas.
experiences.location: Castle Hill (Várhegy), Buda District I, Budapest

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Eastern Europe — Prague & Budapest
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: N/A — Flight arrives at 22:30
day_by_day.afternoon: N/A — In transit
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Prague Václav Havel Airport at 22:30. Take the budget-friendly Airport Express bus (Line AE) or night bus to the city center. Check in to your accommodation, drop off luggage, and take a short relaxing walk around the immediate neighborhood to get oriented. Grab a late-night snack from a nearby convenience store or 24-hour kebab shop.

meals.breakfast: On the plane or at the airport
meals.lunch: On the plane or at the airport
meals.dinner: Late-night street food or convenience store near accommodation — budget ~€3–5

day_by_day.notes: Keep energy low on arrival night. Confirm public transport options from the airport in advance. Night bus B or Line AE runs regularly and costs under €2. Have Czech koruna (CZK) or a card ready for transport.

day_by_day.morning: Start with a slow morning and a budget breakfast near your accommodation. Head to Prague Old Town (Staré Město) on foot or by tram. Visit the iconic Old Town Square, admire the Astronomical Clock (Orloj) — free to view from outside — and explore the Gothic Týn Church exterior. Wander the cobblestone streets and soak in the medieval atmosphere.
day_by_day.afternoon: Cross the famous Charles Bridge (free) for stunning views of the Vltava River and Prague Castle on the hill. Explore Malá Strana (Lesser Town) at the foot of the castle — browse local artisan stalls and enjoy the charming baroque streets. Visit St. Nicholas Church in Malá Strana (small entrance fee ~€2). Climb up to Prague Castle complex — the courtyards and St. Vitus Cathedral exterior are free to access.
day_by_day.evening: Head back to Old Town for the golden-hour atmosphere. Stroll along the riverside promenade. Enjoy a budget Czech dinner at a local pivnice (beer hall) — try svíčková (beef sirloin in cream sauce) or goulash with bread dumplings.

meals.breakfast: Local bakery or café near accommodation — try a párek v rohlíku (Czech hot dog) or pastry — budget ~€2–3
meals.lunch: Street food at Old Town Square or a cheap sandwich from a local bakery — budget ~€4–6
meals.dinner: Traditional Czech pivnice (beer hall) such as U Fleků or a local neighborhood pub — budget ~€8–12 including a Czech beer

day_by_day.notes: Wear comfortable walking shoes — Prague is very walkable but hilly near the castle. Tram Day Pass costs ~€3.50 CZK equivalent and is worth it for multiple rides. Most major sights are free or low-cost to view from the outside.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Josefov, Prague's historic Jewish Quarter. Walk through the exterior of the Old Jewish Cemetery and the synagogues (combined ticket ~€15 — best value for cultural depth). Explore the narrow lanes and learn about the rich Jewish history of Central Europe.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a tram or walk to Vinohrady or Žižkov neighborhoods — two authentic, less-touristy districts beloved by locals. Visit the quirky Žižkov Television Tower (observation deck ~€8) for panoramic city views. Explore the local street art scene and browse vintage shops in Vinohrady.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Náměstí Míru (Peace Square) in Vinohrady for a lively local atmosphere. Dine at one of the affordable Czech or international restaurants around the square. Try trdelník (chimney cake) from a street vendor as a sweet evening treat.

meals.breakfast: Czech café near accommodation — coffee and toast or a croissant — budget ~€3–4
meals.lunch: Local lunch menu (denní menu) at a Vinohrady neighborhood restaurant — these offer 2-course set lunches for ~€5–7
meals.dinner: Casual restaurant near Náměstí Míru — try fried cheese (smažený sýr) with fries, a Czech classic — budget ~€7–10

day_by_day.notes: The Jewish Quarter combined ticket is the most expensive single item today but is historically invaluable. Denní menu (daily lunch specials) are a Prague budget secret — look for chalkboard signs outside restaurants between 11am–2pm.

day_by_day.morning: Morning visit to Vyšehrad fortress — a lesser-known but stunning hilltop citadel with free entry to the grounds. Explore the neo-Gothic Basilica of St. Peter and Paul (small fee ~€2), the ancient Vyšehrad Cemetery where famous Czechs are buried, and enjoy sweeping views over the Vltava River. Far fewer crowds than Prague Castle.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to the Nusle Valley area and then to Holešovice district — a hip, up-and-coming neighborhood. Visit the DOX Centre for Contemporary Art (~€6) or the Holešovice Market (Holešovická tržnice) for local produce, vintage goods, and street food. Great place to mingle with locals.
day_by_day.evening: Tonight is your last evening in Prague. Return to Old Town for a farewell stroll across Charles Bridge at dusk. Enjoy a final Czech dinner with a classic svíčková or roast duck dish. Consider a budget-friendly Czech craft beer tasting at a local microbrewery bar.

meals.breakfast: Grab a fresh pastry and coffee from a local Holešovice café or market stall — budget ~€3
meals.lunch: Street food at Holešovická tržnice market — try langos (fried dough with toppings) or a grilled sausage — budget ~€4–6
meals.dinner: Farewell Czech dinner at a traditional restaurant in Old Town or Malá Strana — budget ~€10–14 with a beer

day_by_day.notes: Pack your bags tonight for the early morning departure to Budapest tomorrow. Vyšehrad is a hidden gem — arrive early to avoid the small number of tourists that do visit. September weather in Prague is mild (15–20°C), so a light jacket is recommended for evenings.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning departure from Prague to Budapest. The most budget-friendly option is the RegioJet or FlixBus coach (~€10–18 one way, ~7 hours) or a train via Czech/Slovak rail (~€15–25, ~7 hours). Depart by 7–8am to arrive in Budapest by mid-afternoon. Enjoy the scenic Central European countryside along the way.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive in Budapest (Keleti or Népliget station). Check in to your accommodation. Take a gentle orientation walk around your neighborhood. Head to the Great Market Hall (Nagyvásárcsarnok) — a stunning 19th-century iron market hall — to browse local produce, spices, paprika, and Hungarian street food. Great introduction to Budapest's food culture.
day_by_day.evening: Walk along the Pest embankment of the Danube for your first iconic view of Buda Castle and the Chain Bridge illuminated at night. Stroll across the Chain Bridge (free) for panoramic views. Enjoy a budget Hungarian dinner in the Jewish Quarter (District VII) — the city's most vibrant nightlife and food area.

meals.breakfast: Pack snacks or grab food at Prague bus/train station before departure — budget ~€3–5
meals.lunch: Snacks on the coach/train or a quick stop at a service station — budget ~€4–6
meals.dinner: Hungarian lángos (fried flatbread with sour cream and cheese) from a street stall, or a budget étterem (restaurant) in District VII — budget ~€7–10

day_by_day.notes: Book your Prague–Budapest transport in advance online for the best prices. RegioJet coaches are comfortable and often include free Wi-Fi and a drink. Have Hungarian forint (HUF) ready upon arrival — ATMs are widely available at Keleti station. Budapest uses HUF; €1 ≈ ~390 HUF.

day_by_day.morning: Start with Budapest's crown jewel: the Buda Castle District. Take the historic funicular (Sikló) up Castle Hill (~€3 one way) or hike up for free. Explore Buda Castle exterior and the Hungarian National Gallery (free on some days). Walk along Fisherman's Bastion (free for the lower terraces) for the most photogenic panoramic views of the Danube and Parliament building.
day_by_day.afternoon: Descend to the Pest side and visit the Hungarian Parliament Building exterior — one of the most beautiful Gothic Revival buildings in Europe. Walk along the iconic Danube Promenade (Duna-korzó). Visit St. Stephen's Basilica (free entry, small fee for tower ~€3) and enjoy views from the dome. Explore the elegant Andrássy Avenue — Budapest's answer to the Champs-Élysées.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the Jewish Quarter (Erzsébetváros, District VII). Visit the stunning Great Synagogue on Dohány Street (exterior free, interior ~€7) — the largest synagogue in Europe. Dine at one of the affordable Jewish Quarter restaurants or try a ruin bar (romkocsma) like Szimpla Kert for a unique cultural experience and cheap drinks.

meals.breakfast: Local Hungarian café — try kürtőskalács (chimney cake) or a fresh pogácsa (savory scone) with coffee — budget ~€3–4
meals.lunch: Affordable étterem near the Parliament — try gulyás (goulash soup) with bread — budget ~€5–8
meals.dinner: Jewish Quarter ruin bar or nearby restaurant — try lángos, kürtős, or a Hungarian pörkölt (stew) — budget ~€8–12

day_by_day.notes: Sunday mornings are magical in Budapest with fewer crowds. The ruin bars of the Jewish Quarter are a uniquely Budapest cultural phenomenon — Szimpla Kert also hosts a Sunday farmers market in the morning, perfect for budget browsing and local snacks.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Heroes' Square (Hősök tere) — completely free and one of Hungary's most important monuments. Explore the adjacent City Park (Városliget) — a beautiful green space with the fairytale Vajdahunyad Castle (free exterior, small museum fee inside ~€4). A perfect morning for a slow, scenic walk.
day_by_day.afternoon: Treat yourself to a quintessential Budapest experience: a thermal bath. Visit Széchenyi Thermal Bath in City Park (~€20–25 for a full day pass) — one of the largest and most beautiful thermal bath complexes in Europe. Spend 2–3 hours soaking in the outdoor and indoor pools. This is a budget-friendly luxury unique to Budapest.
day_by_day.evening: Head to the lively Gozsdu Udvar courtyard in the Jewish Quarter for evening food and drinks. Browse the street food stalls and local bars. Try chimney cake ice cream (a Budapest trend), kürtős, or a hearty Hungarian kürtőskalács. End the night with a scenic walk across the Liberty Bridge (Szabadság híd) — free and beautifully lit at night.

meals.breakfast: Café near City Park or a local pékség (bakery) — fresh bread roll with butter and coffee — budget ~€2–4
meals.lunch: Pack a picnic from a local supermarket (Aldi, Lidl, or Spar) to enjoy in City Park — budget ~€4–6
meals.dinner: Gozsdu Udvar street food or a nearby budget restaurant — try halászlé (fisherman's soup) or stuffed peppers — budget ~€8–11

day_by_day.notes: Bring a swimsuit, towel, and flip-flops for the thermal bath. Lockers are available for rent. Széchenyi is the most iconic but Rudas or Lukács baths are slightly cheaper alternatives. The thermal bath experience is a cultural must-do in Budapest and worth the splurge.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Budapest. Visit the Citadella on Gellért Hill (free hike up, about 20–30 minutes) for the best panoramic views of the entire city — both Buda and Pest, the Danube, all the bridges, and the Parliament. A perfect farewell view. Stop at the Liberty Statue (Szabadság-szobor) at the top.
day_by_day.afternoon: Descend to the Gellért Baths area and explore the charming Tabán neighborhood at the foot of the hill. Browse the Central European University area or visit a local antique market if one is running. Do any last-minute souvenir shopping — pick up Hungarian paprika, Tokaji wine, or handmade folk crafts from the Great Market Hall (revisit if needed). Head to the airport or station for your departure.
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Budapest. If your flight/train is late evening, enjoy a final farewell Hungarian meal near the city center before heading to the airport (Budapest Ferenc Liszt International Airport — BUD) via the 100E airport bus (~€3) or train.

meals.breakfast: Final Hungarian breakfast at a local café — try a traditional Hungarian breakfast plate with salami, cheese, eggs, and paprika — budget ~€4–6
meals.lunch: Quick and affordable lunch near the Great Market Hall — try a bowl of gulyás or a fresh lángos — budget ~€5–8
meals.dinner: Final farewell dinner near the city center or airport area — try kürtős, a Hungarian pastry, or a sit-down meal of chicken paprikash — budget ~€8–12

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 2–2.5 hours before your flight for transport to BUD airport. The 100E airport express bus departs from Deák Ferenc tér and takes ~30–40 minutes. Keep some HUF for last-minute transport or snacks. Total estimated daily budget in Budapest: €30–50/day including accommodation, food, transport, and key activities.

trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

day_by_day.morning: No activities — flight in transit
day_by_day.afternoon: No activities — flight in transit
day_by_day.evening: Arrive Prague at 22:30 via Flight UA. Clear customs and immigration, collect luggage, and transfer to your hotel. Take the Airport Express Bus (Line AE) to Hlavní nádraží (Main Train Station) for ~60 CZK, then a short taxi or rideshare to your accommodation. Check in, freshen up, and unwind.

meals.breakfast: On the plane or at the airport
meals.lunch: On the plane or at the airport
meals.dinner: If hungry upon arrival, grab a late-night bite at a 24-hour spot near the hotel or order room service. Try Lokál Hamburk (open late) for a Czech beer and svíčková if accessible.

day_by_day.notes: Keep Day 1 light — you've just landed after 22:30. Prioritize rest for the full days ahead. Exchange some currency to Czech Koruna (CZK) at the airport, but avoid airport exchange booths with poor rates; use an ATM instead.

day_by_day.morning: Start your Prague exploration with a visit to Prague Castle (Pražský hrad) — one of the largest ancient castles in the world. Explore St. Vitus Cathedral, the Old Royal Palace, and Golden Lane. Arrive early (~9:00 AM) to beat the crowds. Purchase a combined ticket (~350 CZK) for full access.
day_by_day.afternoon: Descend from the castle through the charming Malá Strana (Lesser Town) neighborhood. Cross the iconic Charles Bridge, admiring the Baroque statues and panoramic views of the Vltava River. Continue into Staré Město (Old Town) and visit the Old Town Square, watching the Astronomical Clock (Orloj) chime at the top of the hour.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll through the Jewish Quarter (Josefov) at dusk for atmospheric views, then head to a traditional Czech restaurant for dinner. Afterward, enjoy an evening walk along the illuminated Charles Bridge.

meals.breakfast: Café Louvre or your hotel café — try a Czech-style breakfast with eggs, cold cuts, and fresh bread (~150–200 CZK)
meals.lunch: Nase Maso — a beloved local butcher-restaurant in Old Town; try the beef tartare or goulash sandwich (~200–300 CZK)
meals.dinner: Lokál Dlouhááá — an authentic Czech pub-restaurant; order svíčková (beef sirloin with cream sauce), roast duck, or beef goulash with bread dumplings, paired with a Pilsner Urquell draft (~400–600 CZK)

day_by_day.notes: Wear comfortable walking shoes — Prague Castle involves significant uphill walking and cobblestones. September weather is mild (15–22°C), so a light jacket is recommended for the evening.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Vyšehrad Fortress, a lesser-visited but historically rich castle complex overlooking the Vltava River. Explore the neo-Gothic Basilica of St. Peter and St. Paul, the Vyšehrad Cemetery (resting place of Czech luminaries like Dvořák and Mucha), and enjoy sweeping city views from the ramparts — all largely free of charge.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Vinohrady and Žižkov neighborhoods — two of Prague's most authentic residential districts. Visit the quirky Žižkov Television Tower (with baby sculptures by David Černý), browse the Náměstí Míru square, and explore local boutiques and galleries. Stop by the National Museum (Národní muzeum) on Wenceslas Square for a dose of Czech history (~200 CZK entry).
day_by_day.evening: Attend a classical music concert or opera at the Estates Theatre (Stavovské divadlo) — where Mozart himself premiered Don Giovanni in 1787. Book tickets in advance online (~500–1,200 CZK depending on performance). Alternatively, enjoy live jazz at Jazz Dock along the riverbank.

meals.breakfast: Eska Bakery in Karlín district — known for sourdough bread, pastries, and excellent coffee (~150–200 CZK)
meals.lunch: Café Savoy in Malá Strana — elegant yet mid-range; try the Czech onion soup and schnitzel (~350–500 CZK)
meals.dinner: Pre-concert dinner at Café Imperial — a stunning Art Nouveau brasserie; try the roasted duck leg or beef tartare (~500–700 CZK)

day_by_day.notes: Book Estates Theatre tickets at least a few days in advance, especially for September performances. Vyšehrad is a 20-minute tram ride from the city center — take Tram 7 or 18 to the Vyšehrad stop.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip or morning exploration of Kutná Hora (optional): If you're keen on a half-day excursion, take a train from Prague's Main Station (~1 hour, ~120 CZK each way) to visit the famous Sedlec Ossuary (Bone Church) and the magnificent St. Barbara's Cathedral — a UNESCO World Heritage Site. Alternatively, spend the morning exploring Prague's Nové Město (New Town) and Wenceslas Square area at a relaxed pace.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Prague (or continue from New Town) and visit the Mucha Museum dedicated to Art Nouveau master Alfons Mucha (~240 CZK). Then browse the Palladium Shopping Centre or the artisan shops along Pařížská Street. Head to the Letná Park (Letenské sady) for panoramic views over the city and the Vltava River — a favorite local hangout.
day_by_day.evening: This is your last evening in Prague — make it memorable. Take a one-hour Vltava River cruise at sunset (~400–600 CZK) to see Prague's skyline glittering in the golden hour. Then pack your bags for the morning transfer to Budapest.

meals.breakfast: Mamacoffee — a local specialty coffee chain with great pastries and sandwiches (~150 CZK)
meals.lunch: If in Kutná Hora: Pivnice Dačický — a historic pub with Czech classics like pork knuckle and dark beer (~300–400 CZK). If in Prague: Kantýna — a modern Czech canteen with excellent grilled meats (~300–400 CZK)
meals.dinner: Field Restaurant — a celebrated farm-to-table Czech restaurant in Old Town; splurge slightly for your farewell Prague dinner (~700–1,000 CZK for a tasting experience)

day_by_day.notes: If doing the Kutná Hora day trip, take the 8:00–9:00 AM train to maximize time there and return by early afternoon. Pack light for the train ride. Confirm your Budapest train or bus booking for Day 5 travel.

day_by_day.morning: Check out of your Prague hotel and travel to Budapest by train or bus. The most scenic and popular route is the RegioJet or FlixBus (~4.5–7 hours, €15–35 depending on booking). Trains depart from Praha Hlavní nádraží (Main Station). Enjoy the Central European countryside views along the way. Alternatively, a direct train (Czech Railways + Hungarian Railways) takes ~7 hours with a scenic route through Bratislava.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive in Budapest in the early-to-mid afternoon. Check in to your Budapest accommodation. Get your bearings with a walk through the vibrant Pest side — stroll along Váci Street and the Danube Promenade (Duna-korzó), catching your first views of the Buda Castle across the river.
day_by_day.evening: Ease into Budapest with a visit to the iconic Great Market Hall (Nagy Vásárcsarnok) — even if it's closing time, the exterior is stunning. Then head to the Jewish Quarter (VII. District) around Kazinczy Street for Budapest's famous ruin bar scene. Visit Szimpla Kert — the original and most famous ruin bar — for a drink and to soak in the eclectic atmosphere.

meals.breakfast: Light breakfast at Prague hotel or grab a pastry and coffee at the train station before departure
meals.lunch: On the train — pack snacks from a Prague supermarket (Albert or Billa) or buy from the onboard bistro car (~200–300 CZK)
meals.dinner: Frici Papa Kifőzdéje — a beloved, no-frills Hungarian canteen in Budapest's Pest side; try gulyás (goulash soup), chicken paprikash, or stuffed peppers (~2,500–3,500 HUF)

day_by_day.notes: Book your Prague–Budapest train or bus ticket in advance online (RegioJet.com or FlixBus.com) for the best prices. Arrive at the station 30 minutes early. Exchange some cash to Hungarian Forint (HUF) upon arrival — Budapest is still largely cash-friendly.

day_by_day.morning: Explore Buda Castle Hill — take the historic Funicular (Budavári Sikló, ~1,400 HUF return) or walk up for free. Visit Buda Castle (Magyar Nemzeti Galéria — Hungarian National Gallery, ~3,200 HUF) and the Budapest History Museum. Walk along the Fisherman's Bastion (Halászbástya) — free to walk around the outer terraces — and admire the neo-Gothic Matthias Church (Mátyás-templom, ~2,500 HUF entry).
day_by_day.afternoon: Descend from Castle Hill and cross the Chain Bridge (Széchenyi Lánchíd) on foot — one of the most photogenic bridges in Europe. Explore the Pest side: visit St. Stephen's Basilica (Szent István Bazilika, ~1,000 HUF suggested donation) and take the elevator to the dome for panoramic city views. Walk along Andrássy Avenue, a UNESCO-listed boulevard lined with Neo-Renaissance mansions.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a performance at the Hungarian State Opera House (Magyar Állami Operaház) — one of the most beautiful opera houses in the world. Tickets range from ~3,000–15,000 HUF. Book in advance at opera.hu. Alternatively, take a night cruise on the Danube (~5,000–7,000 HUF) for illuminated views of the Parliament and bridges.

meals.breakfast: New York Café — a legendary, ornate café often called 'the world's most beautiful café'; try the Hungarian breakfast with eggs, cold cuts, and pastries (~3,500–5,000 HUF — a worthwhile splurge for the atmosphere)
meals.lunch: Borkonyha Winekitchen (near Basilica) — a Michelin Bib Gourmand restaurant with excellent Hungarian cuisine at reasonable prices; try the foie gras or beef cheeks (~4,000–6,000 HUF)
meals.dinner: Gerloczy Bistro near Városháza Park — cozy Austro-Hungarian bistro; try the chicken paprikash with nokedli (egg dumplings) or the veal stew (~3,000–5,000 HUF)

day_by_day.notes: Sunday mornings can be quieter at Buda Castle — ideal timing. The Fisherman's Bastion is most magical in the morning light. Wear comfortable shoes for the cobblestones on Castle Hill.

day_by_day.morning: Start with a quintessential Budapest experience — a visit to the Széchenyi Thermal Baths (Széchenyi Gyógyfürdő) in City Park. This stunning Neo-Baroque bathhouse is one of the largest in Europe. Enjoy the outdoor and indoor thermal pools, steam rooms, and saunas. Entry with locker: ~8,000–10,000 HUF. Arrive by 9:00 AM to enjoy it before crowds build.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore City Park (Városliget) surrounding the baths. Visit Vajdahunyad Castle (free entry to grounds) and the Museum of Fine Arts (Szépművészeti Múzeum, ~4,200 HUF) if interested in European art. Then head to the Hungarian Parliament Building (Országház) — the world's third-largest parliament. Book a guided tour in advance (~8,000 HUF) for access to the interior, including the Holy Crown of Hungary.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the Great Synagogue on Dohány Street (Dohány Utcai Zsinagóga) — the largest synagogue in Europe (~5,000 HUF). Afterward, wander the Jewish Quarter's ruin bar district again, this time trying Instant-Fogas or Ellátó Kert for a different vibe. End the evening with a walk along the illuminated Danube embankment.

meals.breakfast: Café near your hotel or Molnár's Kürtőskalács — grab a chimney cake (kürtőskalács) and coffee as a quintessential Hungarian street breakfast (~800–1,200 HUF)
meals.lunch: Bagolyvár Restaurant in City Park — a charming, mid-range Hungarian restaurant near the baths; try the cold sour cherry soup (meggyleves) and stuffed cabbage (~4,000–6,000 HUF)
meals.dinner: Menza Restaurant on Liszt Ferenc Square — a retro-chic Hungarian restaurant; try the goose liver, beef goulash, or the Hungarian lángos appetizer (~3,500–5,500 HUF)

day_by_day.notes: Bring a swimsuit, towel (or rent one at the baths for ~1,000 HUF), and flip-flops for Széchenyi. Parliament tours sell out — book online at latogatokozpont.parlament.hu at least 2–3 days ahead. Monday is a quieter day at most museums.

day_by_day.morning: Spend your final morning at the Budapest Central Market Hall (Nagy Vásárcsarnok) — a magnificent 19th-century iron-and-glass market hall. Browse the ground floor for fresh Hungarian produce, paprika, salami, and Tokaji wine. The upper floor has folk crafts, embroidery, and souvenirs — perfect for last-minute gifts. Then take a final stroll along the Danube embankment and the 'Shoes on the Danube Bank' Holocaust memorial.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on your departure time, visit the Hungarian National Museum (Magyar Nemzeti Múzeum, ~2,800 HUF) for a comprehensive overview of Hungary's 1,000-year history. Alternatively, explore the trendy Ráday Street café culture in the IX. District or take a leisurely walk through the Palace Quarter (Palotanegyed). Head to the airport or train station for your onward journey.
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Budapest. If your flight departs late, enjoy a farewell dinner in the city before heading to Budapest Ferenc Liszt International Airport (BUD) — allow 45–60 minutes travel time from the city center via the 100E Airport Express Bus (~1,000 HUF).

meals.breakfast: Ruszwurm Cukrászda in the Castle District (if you have time for a detour) — Budapest's oldest pastry shop since 1827; try the Dobos torte or cream puffs (~1,500–2,000 HUF). Or a café near your hotel for a relaxed final morning.
meals.lunch: Karavan Street Food Court in the Jewish Quarter — an outdoor food truck park with Hungarian and international options; try a lángos (deep-fried flatbread with sour cream and cheese) or a Hungarian sausage (~1,500–2,500 HUF)
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at Costes Downtown (if budget allows for a splurge) — a Michelin-starred restaurant with modern Hungarian cuisine (~15,000–25,000 HUF). For a mid-range option: Buja Disznó — a casual Hungarian bistro known for pork dishes and local wines (~4,000–6,000 HUF)

day_by_day.notes: Allow extra time for souvenir shopping at the Central Market Hall — it gets busy mid-morning. Keep your receipts for VAT refund (if purchases exceed ~54,000 HUF at a single store). Confirm airport transfer logistics the night before. End the trip with a glass of Tokaji Aszú — Hungary's legendary sweet wine — as a perfect farewell toast.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Eastern Europe — Prague & Budapest Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

hotel.name: Aegean Bliss Resort, Eastern Europe — Prague & Budapest

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — late-night arrival at 22:30
day_by_day.afternoon: No activities scheduled — late-night arrival at 22:30
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Prague Václav Havel Airport at 22:30. A pre-arranged private luxury transfer (Mercedes S-Class or similar) whisks you to your hotel in the heart of Prague. Check in, unwind with a welcome drink at the hotel bar, and settle into your premium suite.

meals.breakfast: Not applicable — in-flight or airport dining
meals.lunch: Not applicable — in-flight or airport dining
meals.dinner: Light late-night room service or a nightcap at the hotel's elegant bar upon arrival

day_by_day.notes: Arrange airport meet-and-greet service in advance for a seamless VIP arrival. Confirm hotel late check-in. Keep the first night low-key to rest for a full Day 2 ahead.

day_by_day.morning: Leisurely breakfast at the hotel, then embark on a private guided walking tour of Prague's Old Town (Staré Město). Explore the iconic Old Town Square, the Astronomical Clock (Orloj), and the Gothic Týn Church. Your expert guide will weave in centuries of Bohemian history and hidden architectural gems.
day_by_day.afternoon: Cross the legendary Charles Bridge on foot, admiring the 30 Baroque statues lining the bridge. Continue uphill to Prague Castle (Pražský hrad) — the largest ancient castle complex in the world. Tour St. Vitus Cathedral, the Royal Palace, and the Golden Lane with your private guide. Enjoy sweeping panoramic views of the city's red-rooftop skyline.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails at a rooftop bar in Malá Strana (Lesser Town) with views of the illuminated castle. Followed by a fine-dining dinner at a celebrated Prague restaurant focusing on modern Czech cuisine with premium wine pairings.

meals.breakfast: Gourmet à la carte breakfast at the hotel — fresh pastries, smoked salmon, eggs Benedict, and specialty Czech coffee
meals.lunch: Elegant lunch at Lokál Dlouhááá or a comparable upscale Czech brasserie near Old Town — try svíčková (beef sirloin) and Pilsner Urquell on tap
meals.dinner: Fine dining at Field Restaurant or La Degustation Bohême Bourgeoise — Michelin-recognized, tasting menu with Czech-inspired contemporary dishes and sommelier-curated wine pairings

day_by_day.notes: Book private guided tours and restaurant reservations well in advance. Wear comfortable walking shoes — Prague's cobblestones are charming but demanding. September weather is typically mild (15–20°C), perfect for outdoor sightseeing.

day_by_day.morning: Private morning visit to the Jewish Quarter (Josefov) — one of the best-preserved Jewish historic districts in Europe. Tour the Old Jewish Cemetery, the Spanish Synagogue (a stunning Moorish Revival masterpiece), and the Pinkas Synagogue with its haunting Holocaust memorial. A knowledgeable guide will bring these stories to life with depth and sensitivity.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Vinohrady and Žižkov neighborhoods — Prague's bohemian, residential side. Visit the striking Žižkov Television Tower (with its famous crawling babies sculptures by David Černý) for panoramic city views. Browse independent galleries and boutiques. Optionally, visit the Mucha Museum dedicated to Art Nouveau master Alfons Mucha.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a world-class classical music concert — Prague is renowned for its music scene. Options include a performance at the Rudolfinum (home of the Czech Philharmonic) or the Estates Theatre (where Mozart himself conducted Don Giovanni in 1787). Pre- and post-concert drinks at a sophisticated cocktail bar.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or a visit to a premium Prague café such as Café Savoy — known for its stunning Neo-Renaissance interior, freshly baked pastries, and excellent coffee
meals.lunch: Lunch at Café Imperial — a landmark Art Deco brasserie with extraordinary mosaic-tiled interiors; try the duck confit or beef tartare
meals.dinner: Pre-concert dinner at Eska — a celebrated farm-to-table restaurant championing Czech ingredients with a modern twist; excellent natural wine list

day_by_day.notes: Book concert tickets well in advance — September is peak season for Prague's classical music calendar. The Jewish Quarter requires a combination ticket; a private guide enhances the experience enormously.

day_by_day.morning: Morning day trip to Český Krumlov or Kutná Hora (both approximately 1–1.5 hours from Prague by private car). Recommended: Kutná Hora — a UNESCO World Heritage town featuring the extraordinary Sedlec Ossuary (Bone Church), adorned with chandeliers and decorations made from human bones, and the stunning Gothic Cathedral of St. Barbara.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring Kutná Hora's beautifully preserved medieval town center, the Italian Court (former royal mint), and the Stone Fountain. Alternatively, if Český Krumlov is chosen, tour its fairytale castle, Baroque theater, and the serpentine Vltava River valley. Private driver waits throughout.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Prague by private car. Freshen up at the hotel, then enjoy a leisurely evening stroll across Charles Bridge at dusk — magical under the golden evening light. Dinner at an intimate, upscale restaurant in Malá Strana.

meals.breakfast: Early hotel breakfast before departure
meals.lunch: Lunch in Kutná Hora at Restaurace Ruthardka or a comparable local restaurant — try regional Czech specialties in a historic setting
meals.dinner: Dinner at Terasa U Zlaté Studně (Terrace at the Golden Well) — a rooftop restaurant with breathtaking castle views and refined Czech-European cuisine; one of Prague's most romantic dining experiences

day_by_day.notes: Arrange a private driver/car for the full day for maximum comfort and flexibility. The Sedlec Ossuary is a genuinely unique and thought-provoking experience — not to be missed. Return to Prague by early evening to avoid fatigue.

day_by_day.morning: Premium private transfer (luxury car or scenic train in first class) from Prague to Budapest — approximately 7 hours by train or 4.5 hours by car/plane. Recommended: a scenic first-class train journey through Central European countryside, or a short 1-hour flight for maximum efficiency. Arrive in Budapest by midday.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check in to your luxury Budapest hotel. After settling in, begin exploring with a private guided tour of the Buda Castle District (Castle Hill) — a UNESCO World Heritage Site. Visit Matthias Church with its stunning geometric tile roof, the Fisherman's Bastion for iconic panoramic views over the Danube and Pest, and the medieval Royal Palace complex.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cruise on the Danube River aboard a private or small-group luxury boat — Budapest's illuminated skyline (Parliament, Chain Bridge, Buda Castle) is considered one of the most spectacular river views in the world. Champagne and canapés on board.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast in Prague before departure
meals.lunch: First-class dining car on the train, or a stylish lunch stop en route if traveling by car
meals.dinner: Welcome dinner in Budapest at Costes Downtown or Onyx Restaurant — both Michelin-starred, offering contemporary Hungarian fine dining with exceptional tasting menus and wine pairings

day_by_day.notes: Book the Budapest hotel and dinner reservations well in advance — September is high season. The Danube evening cruise is best booked as a private charter for a truly premium experience. Confirm luggage transfer arrangements between cities.

day_by_day.morning: Indulge in Budapest's legendary thermal spa culture. Begin the morning with a private or VIP session at Széchenyi Thermal Bath (the largest medicinal bath in Europe) or the ornate Gellért Baths — both architectural masterpieces. Enjoy the thermal pools, steam rooms, and optional massage treatments in a relaxed, luxurious setting.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private guided tour of Pest's grand boulevards. Visit the Hungarian Parliament Building (one of Europe's largest and most ornate parliament buildings) — arrange an interior tour for access to the Crown Jewels and ceremonial halls. Stroll along Andrássy Avenue (Budapest's Champs-Élysées) to Heroes' Square and the City Park (Városliget), home to Vajdahunyad Castle.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the vibrant Jewish Quarter (the 7th district) — Budapest's cultural and nightlife hub. Visit the Great Synagogue on Dohány Street (the largest synagogue in Europe). Browse the ruin bars and atmospheric streets before a sophisticated dinner nearby.

meals.breakfast: Leisurely gourmet breakfast at the hotel before heading to the baths
meals.lunch: Elegant lunch at Gerbeaud Café on Vörösmarty Square — Budapest's most iconic and historic café, famous for its exquisite cakes, pastries, and refined Hungarian lunch menu
meals.dinner: Dinner at Babel Budapest — a celebrated restaurant offering innovative Hungarian cuisine using seasonal, locally sourced ingredients; exceptional wine list featuring Hungarian Tokaj and Eger wines

day_by_day.notes: Book spa treatments in advance, especially on weekends. The Hungarian Parliament tour must be booked ahead — timed entry slots fill quickly. The Jewish Quarter is best explored on foot in the early evening when the atmosphere is particularly vibrant.

day_by_day.morning: Private day excursion to the Danube Bend (Dunakanyar) — one of Central Europe's most scenic river landscapes, approximately 40–60 minutes from Budapest. Visit the charming Baroque town of Szentendre with its Serbian Orthodox churches, colorful houses, and excellent art galleries and craft shops. Explore the open-air Village Museum (Skanzen) if time permits.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue to Visegrád — a dramatic hilltop castle with sweeping Danube Bend panoramas — and the royal town of Esztergom, home to Hungary's largest cathedral and the birthplace of St. Stephen, Hungary's first king. Private driver and guide throughout for seamless, enriching exploration.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Budapest. Enjoy a relaxing evening — perhaps a private wine tasting experience featuring Hungary's world-class wines: Tokaji Aszú (the 'Wine of Kings'), Egri Bikavér (Bull's Blood), and Villányi reds, guided by a sommelier. Followed by a final grand dinner in Budapest.

meals.breakfast: Early hotel breakfast before departure
meals.lunch: Lunch in Szentendre at a riverside restaurant — try lángos (deep-fried dough with toppings), goulash soup, and Hungarian wines in a picturesque setting
meals.dinner: Farewell Budapest dinner at Stand Restaurant (Michelin-starred) — Chef Szabina Szulló's refined Hungarian tasting menu is a masterclass in local flavors elevated to haute cuisine; pair with a curated Tokaj wine flight

day_by_day.notes: The Danube Bend excursion is best done with a private guide who can tailor the pace and depth of each stop. September light along the Danube is particularly beautiful for photography. Book the wine tasting experience in advance with a reputable sommelier or wine cellar.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Budapest — enjoy a slow, indulgent breakfast at the hotel. Take a last leisurely walk along the Danube Promenade (Duna-korzó) on the Pest side, admiring the Chain Bridge and Buda Castle across the water. Visit the iconic Shoes on the Danube Bank memorial — a poignant and moving Holocaust monument. Browse the Great Market Hall (Nagyvásárcsarnok) for premium Hungarian souvenirs: Tokaji wine, paprika, handmade embroideries, and foie gras.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on departure time: optional visit to the Museum of Fine Arts (Szépművészeti Múzeum) near Heroes' Square — housing one of Central Europe's finest collections of European Old Masters. Or simply relax at the hotel's spa or pool. Private luxury transfer to Budapest Ferenc Liszt International Airport for departure.
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Budapest. Reflect on an extraordinary 8-day journey through two of Central Europe's most magnificent and culturally rich capitals.

meals.breakfast: Luxurious final hotel breakfast — savor every moment with Hungarian pastries, cold cuts, fresh fruit, and specialty coffee
meals.lunch: Light lunch at the Great Market Hall's upper-floor food stalls — try lángos and chimney cake (kürtőskalács) as a final Budapest street food farewell, or dine at a nearby café
meals.dinner: Airport lounge dining or in-flight, depending on departure time

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 3 hours before international departure for airport transfer and check-in. Purchase Hungarian Tokaji Aszú wine at the Great Market Hall or duty-free as a premium souvenir — it travels beautifully. Confirm hotel late checkout if needed to maximize your final morning.
